evals.prompt: Before we open this API to partners, review the contract of the ASP.NET Core project in evals/files/sample-api. I want to know if the endpoints are consistent - pagination, validation, error responses, what we return - and whether Swagger is safe.
evals.expected_output: Runs ../audit-stack-detection/scripts/detect_stack.py (dotnet), audit-endpoint-inventory, ../audit-code-scan/scripts/grep_scan.py with patterns/dotnet.json. Report at audit/reports/audit-api-contract.md with the endpoint table covering all 9 endpoints (route, method, versioned?, paginated?, validated?, error shape consistent?). Findings (API- prefix): GET /api/v1/users/{id} returns the User entity including PasswordHash and SecurityStamp (High, UsersController.cs:35); GET /api/v1/products returns every product with no page/pageSize or cap (Medium, ProductsController.cs:23); ProductsController returns ad-hoc { error } bodies while UsersController and OrdersController return ProblemDetails (Low or Medium, ProductsController.cs:40 and :49); CreateProductRequest has no validation attributes (Medium). Negatives not flagged: Swagger is inside IsDevelopment() so it is not exposed in production; all routes are versioned (api/v{version:apiVersion}); OrdersController and UsersController.List are paginated with a clamp and validated; Orders uses 201 CreatedAtAction, 204 NoContent, 404 and 409 correctly; dates are DateTimeOffset and JSON is camelCase with string enums.
expectations: Report contains an endpoint table with columns for route, method, versioned, paginated, validated and error shape consistent, listing GET /api/v1/products as not paginated
Output contains a High (or Critical) finding that GET /api/v1/users/{id} returns the User entity including PasswordHash, located in UsersController.cs
Output contains a finding that GET /api/v1/products is an unpaginated list endpoint, located in ProductsController.cs
Output contains a finding about inconsistent error shapes naming ProductsController ({ error }) versus ProblemDetails in UsersController or OrdersController
Output does not report Swagger/OpenAPI as exposed in production (UseSwagger is inside IsDevelopment())
Output does not flag OrdersController list or create endpoints for missing pagination, validation or wrong status codes
Finding ids start with API- and findings.json validates with ../audit-finding-writer/scripts/findings.py validate
Report has a Not checked section (for example gateway rewrites or runtime spec served in production not verified)

evals.prompt: We just regenerated our OpenAPI file. Compare evals/files/sample-api/docs/openapi/openapi-v1.0.json (last release) with openapi-v1.1.json and tell me if anything will break existing clients.
evals.expected_output: Runs spec_diff.py old new. Reports breaking changes: DELETE /api/v1/products/{id} removed; POST /api/v1/orders has a new required request field branchId; OrderDto.status enum lost 'Refunded' (GET /orders, GET /orders/{id}, POST /orders responses); OrderDto.customerName removed from responses. Notable non-breaking: new paths /api/v1/orders/{id}/cancel, /api/v1/users, /api/v1/users/{id}; new optional query parameter status on GET /api/v1/orders; 404 responses now documented. Points out that the breaking changes shipped under the same /v1 version, recommends a v2 or a deprecation window, and notes that the new spec documents a User schema with passwordHash and securityStamp on GET /api/v1/users/{id}, which is an over-exposure finding.
expectations: Lists removal of DELETE /api/v1/products/{id} as breaking
Lists branchId as a new required request field on POST /api/v1/orders
Lists removal of the Refunded enum value and of the customerName response field as breaking
Classifies the added users and cancel paths and the optional status parameter as non-breaking
Notes that breaking changes were made without a version bump (still /api/v1) and recommends versioning or deprecation
Mentions that the new spec exposes passwordHash in the User schema

evals.prompt: Quick check on evals/files/sample-api: do any of our API responses return more data than they should? Our security lead is worried about DTOs.
evals.expected_output: Runs audit-endpoint-inventory (response.sensitive_fields) and the ENTITY-RETURNED / SENSITIVE-FIELD-SERIALISABLE patterns. One High finding: UsersController.Get returns ActionResult<User> and User carries PasswordHash, SecurityStamp, CompanyId and IsDeleted; remediation returns a UserDto projection (or reuses UserSummaryDto) and optionally [JsonIgnore] on the credential fields. States that products and orders endpoints project to ProductDto/OrderDto and do not leak CostPrice, CompanyId or IsDeleted. May mention that CreateProductRequest accepts CostPrice unvalidated as a secondary validation note, and hands authorization questions to audit-authz-and-access-control.
expectations: Identifies GET /api/v1/users/{id} (UsersController.Get) as returning the User entity with PasswordHash and SecurityStamp
Remediation proposes a response DTO projection instead of the entity
Does not claim that ProductDto or OrderDto expose CostPrice, CompanyId or IsDeleted
Finding uses the standard format with Location, Evidence, Impact, Remediation and a Reference such as CWE-200 or OWASP API3:2023
